subject: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightwell.com>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwell.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Hi Sanjay / Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise proposal to protect the go-live window while we absorb the remaining eval items:

Summary (short):
- Move the final acceptance window from June 14 -> June 28 (phased cutover: read-only -> restricted write)
- Formalize a 2-week "stabilizer" MAP milestone after initial cutover for performance tuning and KV cache validation
- Offer a capped credit escrow (one-time credit pool) to offset measurable SLA misses tied to production token latency or availability for the first 30 days

Why this helps:
- Preserves your launch target while giving engineering a deterministic runway to validate integrations
- Gives procurement a defined risk bucket (credit escrow) instead of open-ended penalty language

Attachments: updated MAP (v1.3) with milestone dates and acceptance criteria. Also attaching a draft term sheet for the credit escrow for procurement to review.

Ask: Can procurement confirm whether a capped credit escrow is acceptable (cap and signoff owner), and whether the phased dates above are workable for Brightwell stakeholders?

If yes, I can route a redline-friendly SOW appendix and DocuSign the escrow term sheet.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Brightwell_MAP_v1.3.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]
[Attachment: redwood_credit_escrow_term_sheet.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)]

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightwell.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwell.com>
Cc: procurement@brightwell.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Alex —

Thanks for the clear write-up. Two quick items from procurement side: 1) we need a plain-language summary of the credit escrow mechanics (trigger conditions, measurement window, cap), and 2) the legal team prefers accrual-style credits over refunds where possible.

Also, the June 28 phased write cutover is preferable to a single-day cutover if the stabilizer language is explicit. Can you confirm the acceptance criteria you propose for the stabilizer milestone (performance thresholds, KV cache pass rate)?

Sanjay
VP, Platform Ops — Brightwell Systems
[sanjay.rao@brightwell.com | +1 415-555-0198]

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Sanjay —

Agree. Short answers below and attaching a one-page summary for procurement (redwood_credit_escrow_term_sheet.pdf):
- Trigger conditions: measurable SLA breach on 3+ business days within first 30-day post-cutover window where 95th percentile token latency > 600ms or availability < 99.5%
- Measurement: aggregated across production routes defined in the MAP, validated by both parties' telemetry with a simple reconciliation table
- Cap: proposed USD 50k credit pool (applies only to token-cost-equivalent credits for billable usage)
- Acceptance criteria for stabilizer: 95th p latency <= 450ms across representative route samples, KV cache hit rate >= 85% within stabilization window, zero critical error rates for three consecutive 48-hour windows

Attachment: one-pager and updated MAP with the criteria called out in the table.

If procurement can confirm the cap/trigger language is acceptable, we'll prep a short SOW appendix (plain English) and a DocuSign for the escrow.

- Alex

[Attachment: redwood_credit_escrow_term_sheet.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)]
[Attachment: Brightwell_MAP_v1.3.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwell.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightwell.com>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 18 May 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Folks — looping in Jonas (program lead) and Ben (finance) to fast-track the procurement / credit-tracking mechanics.

Internal notes for Brightwell procurement:
- Jonas will own operational acceptance and telemetry reconciliation. He can provide a measurement sheet (CSV) that maps Redwood route IDs to Brightwell route tags for a bilateral validation run.
- Ben will confirm how the credit pool is applied against invoices and produce a short precedent-based memo showing how capped credits are handled in prior deals.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
1) May 20 — procurement confirms cap & accrual preference (Brightwell)
2) May 21 — Redwood sends SOW appendix + DocuSign term sheet
3) May 23 — joint telemetry smoke test and measurement baseline created
4) May 28 — signoff on MAP v1.3 and execute DocuSign

If any of Brightwell's dates are tight, we can compress the joint smoke test to a same-day window. We want to avoid broad redlines that reopen the MAP.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW_appendix_draft.docx (docx, 12 KB)]

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@brightwell.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightwell.com>
Cc: procurement@brightwell.com
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 14:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Marissa / Alex —

Appreciate the clarity. Procurement has reviewed the one-pager and our legal team prefers the following changes before we sign: 1) reduce cap to USD 25k, 2) replace the word "penalty" with "remediation credit" throughout, and 3) require a single reconciliation sign-off from Brightwell operations to release the credit (i.e., we won't do rolling releases).

One ask from procurement: can Redwood provide a simplified SOW appendix that only contains (a) exact milestone dates, (b) the three stabilizer acceptance checks, and (c) the credit escrow mechanics in bullet form? If possible, we need that no later than May 21 to keep our procurement cycle intact.

Regards,
Elena Torres
Sr. Procurement Manager — Brightwell Systems
procurement@brightwell.com

Subject: Re: MAP: phased stabilizer, credit fallback & cordoning plan

Elena / Team —

Thanks — we can accommodate the asks. Final summary below and attachments:

What Redwood will deliver by May 21:
- Simplified SOW appendix (milestone dates, three stabilizer checks, credit mechanics) — SOW_appendix_slim.docx
- DocuSign link for credit escrow with cap reduced to USD 25k and language changed to "remediation credit"
- Measurement reconciliation CSV template for Jonas' acceptance workflow

Proposed final timeline (updated):
- May 21: Redwood sends SOW appendix + DocuSign (action: procurement signature)
- May 23: 2-hour joint telemetry smoke test (Jonas runs and confirms baseline)
- May 28: MAP v1.3 signoff and formal cutover window agreement

If procurement signs the DocuSign by May 24, we will lock the phased window and schedule the joint smoke test. Ben will follow up internally about invoice application of a remediation credit and provide a one-paragraph memo to Brightwell finance.

Closing notes: this preserves the June launch window (phased), avoids open-ended legal language, and gives Brightwell a clear capped remediation vehicle versus disruptive contract redlines.

I'll route the DocuSign now. Link: https://www.docusign.com/link/abcdef123456

- Alex
